title: VPC post-deploy probe playbook and load verifier
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Create an automated post-deploy 'probe playbook' and a lightweight load verifier that runs after Private/VPC deployments. The goal is to provide deterministic, reproducible checks for API readiness, model load behavior, and basic throughput under realistic concurrency. This will be wired into the Terraform deployment pipeline (post-apply hook) and the Deploy Orchestrator so that canaries and full rollouts get validated automatically.

Scope:
- A playbook (set of orchestrated probes) that verifies control-plane APIs, model artifact fetch, model load success, KV-cache priming, and one end-to-end generation smoke test.
- A short-concurrency surge test (30s to 2m) that validates token throughput and latency SLOs under small burst (configurable) to catch mis-sized GPUs / qconfig mismatches.
- Health signal aggregation and a single JSON summary artifact suitable for the CI pipeline and for SAR/incident emails.
- Terraform module hook and a small runner (containerized) that can run in the customer's VPC or in a transient job in our deploy cluster.

Non-goals: long-running stress tests or full load harness; this is a post-deploy verifier, not a performance benchmark suite.
steps: Define probe suite and order: api_ping -> auth_check -> model_artifact_fetch -> model_load -> kv_cache_warm -> generation_smoke -> concurrency_surge
Implement containerized runner (go) that executes probes and emits a normalized JSON summary and Prometheus metrics
Add terraform post-apply hook in private-terraform modules to invoke runner with kubejob or ephemeral VM
Create a lightweight traffic generator that can replay a short prompt set and measure p50/p95 latency and token throughput
Wire alert rules and a dashboard template (Grafana) for quick post-deploy inspection
Document the playbook and CI integration (Confluence) and add to deploy runbooks
acceptance_criteria: Runner container image builds and is published to reg.redwood-inference.dev/images/probe-runner:<sha>
Terraform module exposes a boolean input `enable_postdeploy_verifier` and a `verifier_config` block
A full post-deploy run completes within 5 minutes and produces a JSON summary in S3/MinIO and a Prometheus scrape endpoint
Failure modes are documented and map to actionable remediation (e.g., model pull failure -> check storage IAM; high p95 latency -> consider resizing GPU or quantization mismatch)
Playbook has unit/integration tests in CI and a sample run included in the PR description
